Mental Health Care Plan Details
Principal Problem: Acute migraine-type headache with coexisting anxiety/stress (impact on function)

- Patient Goal(s):
  - Relief from acute headache; improved ability to function at work
  - Reduce anxiety about work deadlines; improve coping with stress

- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Alleviate acute headache symptoms with appropriate analgesia
  - Initiate stress reduction strategies and arrange counselling referral
  - Improve sleep and hydration; assess need for work adjustment

- Actions (Patient):
  - Take Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) as first-line for migraine; continue Paracetamol as tolerated (dose/route/frequency not documented)
  - Improve sleep hygiene and ensure adequate hydration (target 7–8 hours sleep; 1.5–2 liters fluids daily; exclude caffeine)
  - Consider taking time off work (self-certify for one week) to reduce headache triggers
  - Engage with counselling services (self-refer via provided link)
  - Follow up in one week with clinician

- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Prescribe/advise Ibuprofen for migraine-type headache; Paracetamol as adjunct (dose/frequency not documented)
  - Provide link to local counselling service and assist with self-referral
  - Recommend a one-week work absence (self-certification) to reduce stress-triggered headaches
  - Reinforce sleep, hydration, and general self-care recommendations; discuss potential blood tests if no improvement
  - Schedule follow-up in one week; offer earlier contact if symptoms worsen

Secondary Problem: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD)

- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce daily anxiety; maintain functioning at work; enhance coping strategies

- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Review current Sertraline therapy and stability
  - Initiate or optimize access to evidence-based psychotherapy (e.g., CBT)
  - Provide psychoeducation and coping strategies; monitor safety

- Actions (Patient):
  - Continue Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented)
  - Attend counselling/therapy; practice coping strategies discussed
  - Monitor anxiety levels and note triggers

- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Review Sertraline dose, adherence, and side effects (dose not documented)
  - Facilitate referral to psychotherapy (CBT or equivalent)
  - Provide education about anxiety management and relapse prevention
  - Assess need for adjustments to pharmacotherapy or escalation if symptoms worsen

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: migraine vs tension-type headache features, triggers (stress, sleep, hydration), safe analgesia (NSAIDs), hydration and sleep guidelines, danger signs and when to contact a clinician; referral to counselling
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Worsening headache with fever, neck stiffness, new neurological symptoms; increasing anxiety interfering with daily function
- Coping Strategies: Sleep hygiene, hydration, regular meals, gradual return to work plan, coping strategies from counselling, seeking timely follow-up
